Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

Q = 0.368949 on 1 df, I-squared 0.0 per cent, tau-squared 0.0 under REML: the two trials agree closely. THAT AGREEMENT IS NOT THE MAIN UNCERTAINTY HERE. Both trials registered this endpoint as TIME TO FIRST EVENT and this pool combines ODDS RATIOS computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that ran for different lengths of time. AN ODDS RATIO OVER UNEQUAL FOLLOW-UP IS NOT A HAZARD RATIO and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. Direction and rough magnitude are not in doubt -- both favour empagliflozin, both intervals exclude no effect -- but READ THE POOLED NUMBER AS AN APPROXIMATION TO THE QUANTITY THE TRIALS ESTIMATED, NOT AS THAT QUANTITY. Two trials agreeing about an odds ratio over unequal follow-up agree about something neither of them set out to measure.

The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they SHOULD have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason.

How to read this: HOW THIS POOL COMBINES THE TWO TRIALS IS A WEAKER CLAIM THAN WHAT THEY MEASURED. Both trials register the SAME primary endpoint, verified word for word -- the registered strings differ only by the word 'the'. But both register it as TIME TO FIRST EVENT, and this pool combines ODDS RATIOS computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that did not run for the same length of time. AN ODDS RATIO OVER UNEQUAL FOLLOW-UP IS NOT A HAZARD RATIO AND DOES NOT BECOME ONE BY BEING POOLED: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume they mean. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. The direction and rough magnitude here are not in doubt -- both trials favour empagliflozin and both intervals exclude no effect -- but the pooled number should be read as an approximation to the quantity the trials estimated, not as that quantity. Recorded 2026-08-20. Whether this pool is recomputed from the published hazard ratios is a decision that has been referred and not taken; the limitation is stated either way, because a reader must not be able to reach the estimate without meeting it.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 8. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML0.7576 (0.6825 to 0.8409)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.7576 (0.385 to 1.4907)

The published point is 0.7576 and the house-rule point is 0.7576. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives. AND BOTH INTERVALS IN THIS TABLE BRACKET AN ODDS RATIO COMPUTED OVER UNEQUAL FOLLOW-UP. Both trials registered this endpoint as time to first event; this pool combines odds ratios from cumulative arm counts over trials of different duration, and AN ODDS RATIO OVER UNEQUAL FOLLOW-UP IS NOT A HAZARD RATIO and does not become one by being pooled. Which of these two interval methods is preferred is a smaller question than which quantity is being bracketed.

A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.

Abstract

Question. In adults with heart failure, does empagliflozin compared with placebo reduce the first occurrence of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalisation for heart failure -- the outcome BOTH trials register as their primary?1

Methods. eligibility was not recorded on the page this object was extracted from; estimates were pooled under random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials), 22 August 2019 version as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook; and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) | Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF): odds ratio 0.758 (0.682 to 0.841) across 2 trials; and heterogeneity was closely (I-squared 0%).3

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In adults with heart failure, does empagliflozin compared with placebo reduce the first occurrence of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalisation for heart failure -- the outcome BOTH trials register as their primary? It pools 2 randomised trials, against placebo. The outcome pooled is Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) | Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF). Everything in this paragraph is derived from stored fields and none of it is authored. The interpretive sentences that follow are marked as drafts and are the author's to replace.

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Why the question is still open -- the specific uncertainty this review addresses. The evidence identified on this question is 2 randomised trials (NCT03057951, NCT03057977), pooled here at 0.758 (95% CI 0.682 to 0.841) for primary. Certainty in that estimate is rated LOW. WHICH OF THOSE UNRESOLVED POINTS MAKES THE QUESTION WORTH ASKING NOW IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.2

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Why a NEW synthesis is warranted rather than citing an existing one. A search for published syntheses matched an unrecorded number of record(s); an unrecorded number were read and an unrecorded number appraised against this review. The appraised synthesis is an untitled record. WHETHER THOSE DIFFERENCES WARRANT A NEW SYNTHESIS RATHER THAN CITING THE EXISTING ONE IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.3

Results

The pooled odds ratio for multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to the First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) | Time to First Event of Adjudicated Cardiovascular (CV) Death or Adjudicated Hospitalisation for Heart Failure (HHF) was 0.758 (0.682 to 0.841) across 2 trials, against placebo.1

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.369, on degrees of freedom 1. Q = 0.368949 on 1 df, I-squared 0.0 per cent, tau-squared 0.0 under REML: the two trials agree closely. THAT AGREEMENT IS NOT THE MAIN UNCERTAINTY HERE. Both trials registered this endpoint as TIME TO FIRST EVENT and this pool combines ODDS RATIOS computed from cumulative arm counts, over trials that ran for different lengths of time. AN ODDS RATIO OVER UNEQUAL FOLLOW-UP IS NOT A HAZARD RATIO and does not become one by being pooled: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights do not mean what a reader would assume. Both trials published a hazard ratio and those are the right inputs. Direction and rough magnitude are not in doubt -- both favour empagliflozin, both intervals exclude no effect -- but READ THE POOLED NUMBER AS AN APPROXIMATION TO THE QUANTITY THE TRIALS ESTIMATED, NOT AS THAT QUANTITY. Two trials agreeing about an odds ratio over unequal follow-up agree about something neither of them set out to measure.2

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: The extractor recovered a pooled result from this page, so the page pooled these trials. Whether they SHOULD have been pooled is not established by conversion - several pages in this corpus pooled harm with efficacy, or distinct agents, and their estimates were withdrawn for that reason. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.3

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.4

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials), 22 August 2019 version as reproduced in the Cochrane Handbook. The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources READ is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION. 2

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT WAS OBTAINED FROM: GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family) -- the assessment above4

How the second assessor was asked: BLIND, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py. The prompt is assembled from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and REFUSES to send if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed.5

THE DISAGREEMENT RATE, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 6 of 12 judgements -- 50.0%. Reported as DISAGREEMENT: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.6

7The second assessor's reply, verbatim: NCT03057951__primary D1=NO_INFORMATION D2=NO_INFORMATION D3=NO_INFORMATION D4=LOW D5=LOW OVERALL=NO_INFORMATION NCT03057977__primary D1=NO_INFORMATION D2=NO_INFORMATION D3=NO_INFORMATION D4=LOW D5=LOW OVERALL=NO_INFORMATION

The facts both assessors were shown -- a rate is meaningless without them: A DISAGREEMENT RATE IS MEANINGLESS WITHOUT THE FACTS BOTH ASSESSORS SAW, so the list is stated here the way a denominator is stated. Fields emitted: trial, cohort, registered enrolment, registered masking, registered sites, registered comparator, number of registered arms, number of registered PRIMARY outcomes, registered PRIMARY outcome, registered analysis population, the rank the pooled result holds, the result being assessed, participants this review pools, registered enrolment minus participants pooled. Established by test, not argument: widening this list from 9 fields to 14 HALVED gepotidacin's disagreement -- its entire D5 divergence was a fact the second assessor had never been shown -- and left ceftaroline and tigecycline unmoved.8

Where they disagree, by domain: D1 2 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 2 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree and OVERALL 2 of 2 disagree.9

That rate was measured before this review's D1 judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's D1 judgements moved from LOW to NO_INFORMATION on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.10

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 4 of 12 judgements -- 33.3%. By domain: D1 0 of 2 disagree, D2 0 of 2 disagree, D3 2 of 2 disagree, D4 0 of 2 disagree, D5 0 of 2 disagree and OVERALL 2 of 2 disagree.11

2 D1 judgement(s) on this topic moved. Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.. 1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect or a dose-response gradient applies to observational evidence that has not already been rated down, and neither condition holds here.2

Certainty LOW. The risk-of-bias domain reads the per-result RoB 2 assessments made 2026-08-20 and named above, not a topic-level summary; indirectness reads the estimand findings recorded on this pool.3

Discussion

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the effect size is clinically meaningful. The pooled OR is 0.758 (95% CI 0.682 to 0.841) over 2 trials. Certainty is rated LOW. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. WHETHER A CHANGE OF THAT MAGNITUDE IS CLINICALLY MEANINGFUL IN THIS POPULATION IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT: NO FIELD ON THIS OBJECT RECORDS A THRESHOLD OF IMPORTANCE, AND NONE IS ASSUMED HERE.1

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- Whether the observed heterogeneity is clinically important. Across 2 trials, tau-squared 0; every trial interval excludes no effect. WHETHER THAT DEGREE OF DISAGREEMENT MATTERS CLINICALLY -- WHETHER THE TRIALS ARE ANSWERING THE SAME QUESTION IN THE SAME PATIENTS -- IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.2

DRAFT FOR THE AUTHOR TO REPLACE -- WHY this result differs from the published ones, mechanically or methodologically. This review pools 0.758 (95% CI 0.682 to 0.841) over 2 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled an outcome not recorded here. Which trials that synthesis carries: Both contributing trials are keyed to a verified ClinicalTrials.gov registration -- NCT03057977 and NCT03057951 -- each carrying the registry's own posted primary-outcome title on this object, BEFORE any count was compared with anyone else's. A k that agrees is not a k that matches. WHY THE TWO RESULTS DIFFER -- WHETHER BY POPULATION, OUTCOME DEFINITION, MODEL OR INCLUDED SET -- IS THE AUTHOR'S JUDGEMENT.3

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities; query, counts and a per-record decision in ssot/empagliflozin-hf-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json. 130 records matched, 25 retrieved, 5 appraised, 125 NOT READ. NO INCLUDED-STUDY TABLE WAS READ for any of the five: their trial sets are INFERRED from abstract text, participant totals and search cut-off dates, and every check resting on an inferred set says so.1

This review was compared against 3 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

3What this comparison found. State. A FINDING ABOUT THE EVIDENCE, NOT A COMPARISON OUTCOME What. NO IDENTIFIED SYNTHESIS POOLS EMPEROR-REDUCED WITH EMPEROR-PRESERVED ON THIS ENDPOINT, and the reason is mechanical rather than mysterious. Why the gap exists. The closest empagliflozin-only synthesis (Pan 2021) CLOSED ITS SEARCH ON 20 JANUARY 2021 and EMPEROR-Preserved reported in August 2021, so the second trial could not have been in it. The nearest synthesis that DOES contain EMPEROR-Preserved (Banerjee 2023) is restricted to mildly reduced and preserved ejection fraction, which EXCLUDES EMPEROR-Reduced -- half of this review. One is seven months too early; the other excludes half the evidence. That is a specific account of the gap, and it is far stronger than reporting an absence. So what it means. This review's estimate is NEITHER CORROBORATED NOR CONTRADICTED by the identified literature. IT IS UNREPLICATED. A reader should not take the direction agreeing across every published figure as independent support, because no published figure is answering this question. And closeness is not corroboration. Banerjee's HR 0.80 (0.74 to 0.86) sits close to this review's OR 0.7576 (0.6825 to 0.8409), and THAT CLOSENESS MEANS NOTHING. Different drug set -- class-wide against empagliflozin alone. Different population -- preserved and mildly reduced ejection fraction against the whole spectrum. Different measure -- a hazard ratio against an odds ratio over unequal follow-up. TWO NUMBERS THAT ARE CLOSE WHILE ANSWERING DIFFERENT QUESTIONS ARE THE THING THIS REVIEW EXISTS TO REFUSE, not evidence for it. It is recorded as UNRESOLVED in the check table for exactly that reason. The bound on this claim. It is 'NO IDENTIFIED SYNTHESIS', never 'no synthesis'. The screen matched 130 records, retrieved 25, appraised 5 and DID NOT READ 125. A synthesis pooling this pair could exist among them. And no included-study table was read for any of the five appraised, so even their trial sets are inferred from abstract text, participant totals and search cut-off dates.

On what basis their trial set is known: Both contributing trials are keyed to a verified ClinicalTrials.gov registration -- NCT03057977 and NCT03057951 -- each carrying the registry's own posted primary-outcome title on this object, BEFORE any count was compared with anyone else's. A k that agrees is not a k that matches.4

Where our result differs from theirs: BY TRIAL SET AND BY MEASURE, AND NOT BY DISAGREEMENT. No identified synthesis pools these two trials together on this endpoint: one predates the second trial, the other excludes the first. Every published figure points the same direction as this review and not one of them is an independent check on it. THE HONEST SUMMARY IS THAT THIS PAIRING IS UNREPLICATED, bounded by the 125 records not read.5

Page standard

UNSTAMPED — unknown-version. This page carries no build_stamp, so the standard it was built to cannot be established. That is a statement about the record, not a claim that the page is below standard.

Every number on this page is projected from a single canonical object, and each measured cell names the source analysis it was read from. That is what is machine-checked. It does not establish that the underlying sources are right, only that this page faithfully reports them.
